title: Smoothness of a Gaussian exponential integral
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Then the function of $x\in\mathbb R^n$ given by $\int f(y)\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(a x_i+b y_i)^2\right)\,d\gamma(y)$ is smooth of every order.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number.
$f$ is integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure.
